cases.statement: One person: patient #4, an Austrian man diagnosed at 72 after low HDL on routine testing, homozygous for c.5055del. Table columns are patients #1 to #4 in order; patient #4 is the fourth value in each row.

people.label: patient #4
people.key_phenotypes: HDL <3 mg/dL and ApoA-I <20 mg/dL; splenomegaly 19.0 cm; thrombocytopenia (platelets 77 G/L); progressive neurodegenerative dementia with intracranial amyloid; triglycerides 468 mg/dL; no reported CAD

quotes.quote: Four male patients were diagnosed with TD at the age of 22 (patient #1) and 72 (patient #4) after low HDL was detected in routine blood tests
| Parameter | Patient #1^a | Patient #2^a | Patient #3 | Patient #4 |
| Mutation (homozygous) | c.2418G > A | c.2418G > A | c.679C > T, p.(Arg227Ter) | c.5055del, p.(Lys1685AsnfsTer9) |
progressive neurodegenerative dementia with evidence of amyloid disposition in relation to large intracranial arteries on magnetic resonance imaging in patient #4
Similarly, patient #4 did not report angina or a history of CAD.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Person-level: undetectable HDL and ApoA-I, splenomegaly and thrombocytopenia (attributed to hypersplenism). The authors say they cannot tell whether patient #4's very high triglycerides are due to TD or other causes. The main text does not describe the genetic test (single gene, panel or exome) or exclusion of other genes; details are said to be in supplemental materials, which are not in the text available here.

quotes.quote: In contrast to the clinical presentation, standard lipid parameters were similar including thrombocytopenia (due to hypersplenism)
However, we have no evidence as to whether these lipid abnormalities are related to his TD manifestation or other causes.
A detailed presentation of all cases is presented in the supplemental materials (17).

segregation.statement: The paper says available, consenting first-degree relatives were genotyped (details in supplementary Fig. S4 / Table 1, not available here), but the main text reports results only for relatives of patients #1-#2 and the son of patient #3. No relative of patient #4 is reported as tested in the main text.

quotes.quote: Specifically, all first-degree relatives that were available and consented to further testing were genotyped for the described variants, and their lipid profiles were analyzed [Supplementary Fig. S4, Supplementary Table 1 (17)].

in_trans.statement: Homozygous per Table 2 and the text. Parental testing and consanguinity for patient #4 are not reported in the main text.

quotes.quote: | Mutation (homozygous) | c.2418G > A | c.2418G > A | c.679C > T, p.(Arg227Ter) | c.5055del, p.(Lys1685AsnfsTer9) |

Genetic testing confirmed homozygous loss-of-function variants in ABCA1 (c.2418G > A in patients #1 and #2, c.679C > T in patient #3, and c.5055del in patient #4, all regarded as American College of Medical Genetics class 5 (pathogenic).

functional.statement: No assay of this variant is reported. The authors state that functional analyses were not available (said of the proposed lipid-metabolism mechanisms).

quotes.quote: Also, discussed mechanisms regulating lipid metabolisms must be regarded as hypotheses, as functional analyses were not available.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Frameshift deletion, predicted NP_005493.2:p.(Lys1685AsnfsTer9) (matches the protein stated in Table 2). The authors call it a loss-of-function variant and describe TD as caused by ABCA1 loss of function.

quotes.quote: Genetic testing confirmed homozygous loss-of-function variants in ABCA1 (c.2418G > A in patients #1 and #2, c.679C > T in patient #3, and c.5055del in patient #4, all regarded as American College of Medical Genetics class 5 (pathogenic).

Specifically, loss-of-function variants in ABCA1 lead to intracellular cholesterol accumulation in the reticuloendothelial system and peripheral macrophages (“foam cells”), which may infiltrate various organs and essentially contribute to the development of atherosclerosis (7).

population_data_in_papers.statement: No frequency data for this variant. The authors state the variant was previously undescribed (novelty statement, not population data).

quotes.quote: Two previously undescribed variants (c.2418G > A, c.5055.del) were reported.
Notably, only c.679C > T has been previously published (18).

authors_classification.statement: Authors classify it as ACMG class 5 (pathogenic); individual ACMG criteria are not listed.

concerns: The paper writes the variant two ways: 'c.5055del' (Results, Table 2) and 'c.5055.del' (Abstract, Discussion).
Transcript not stated in the paper; batch HGVS is on NM_005502.4.
Main-text tables are patient-per-column; values for patient #4 are read from the fourth column.
Patient #4 has features that may have other causes: progressive dementia with intracranial amyloid and very high triglycerides (authors cannot attribute these to TD).
Case details, genetic-testing methods and pedigrees are in supplemental materials (17), which are not part of the text read here.
Homozygosity not confirmed by parental testing in the main text; consanguinity not reported.
notes_for_panel: One elderly homozygous man with biochemically typical TD (undetectable HDL and ApoA-I, splenomegaly, thrombocytopenia), authors' ACMG class 5. No segregation, functional, in-silico or population data for this variant in the main text.
